summary: The repository currently provides generic schema introspection, read-only SQL execution, a pandas-oriented dataset catalog, and a credential-invocation audit ledger—not the proposed accounting contracts. The main gaps are authoritative temporal chart data, cross-dialect execution semantics, fail-closed governance and cache identity, and a package-boundary conflict with the paused semantic-layer specification.

suggestions.title: Make the chart of accounts an immutable, versioned input
suggestions.rationale: `SQLToolkit` introspects table structure but not account values, while `DatasetManagerConfig` only describes data sources. Load-time completeness cannot be proven from information_schema metadata or a live journal table alone. Require an explicit account-master snapshot or manifest, hash it into the model version, and resolve selectors only against that snapshot.

suggestions.title: Use one canonical IR with target-specific SQL renderings
suggestions.rationale: The existing database path is dialect-aware and executes through asyncdb/raw driver connections, while the dataset path is pandas-based. The accepted requirement that identical SQL text run against every source conflicts with dialect rendering and driver parameter conventions. Preserve one canonical accounting IR and emit a separately hashed SQL rendering per target, or explicitly restrict v1 to a tested common SQL subset.

suggestions.title: Do not treat SQLToolkit validation as a semantic allowlist
suggestions.rationale: `validate_query` extracts only FROM/JOIN names and optionally checks cached table metadata; `_check_query_safety` enforces read-only safety, not allowed columns, functions, aliases, or account literals. The accounting compiler needs its own fail-closed AST/resource validation before execution and must authorize the declared journal source before returning SQL.

suggestions.title: Specify the accounting sign contract as data-shape semantics
suggestions.rationale: `amount_sign=by_nature` does not define whether the source amount is a debit-positive value, credit-positive value, or already signed, and account nature alone cannot normalize all journal representations. Require an explicit source shape and normalization rule, preferably with Decimal-compatible types and fixtures for debit, credit, reversal, and signed inputs.

suggestions.title: Validate effective-dated completeness per interval
suggestions.rationale: Selectors have `valid_from`/`valid_to`, but completeness is described as a load-time invariant while the resolved membership depends on the requested period. A single global check can accept gaps or contradictory memberships at a fiscal boundary. Build an interval partition of account-set membership, validate coverage and exclusions for every interval, then compile a period-specific snapshot.

suggestions.title: Fix numeric and empty-result semantics before golden SQL tests
suggestions.rationale: The proposed `SUM(CASE ...)` leaves unmatched groups as NULL, and outer arithmetic can propagate NULL or divide by zero. Exact reconciliation equality is also undefined for floating-point or rounded source amounts. Golden and executable tests must specify COALESCE behavior, Decimal precision, zero denominators, empty periods, negative postings, overlapping sets, and YTD/QTD/MTD boundaries.

suggestions.title: Keep accounting execution separate from the current DatasetManager catalog contract
suggestions.rationale: `DatasetManager.add_dataframe` accepts only pandas, `InMemorySource` returns the original pandas object, and `DatasetInfo.source_type`/`DatasourceSpec` have no accounting-metric kind. Registering finance metrics as ordinary datasets would bypass the proposed Arrow/DuckDB execution and PBAC semantics. Introduce a dedicated accounting runner/catalog adapter, or explicitly extend these contracts and their policy tests before integration.

suggestions.title: Exclude shared DatasetManager caches from accounting results
suggestions.rationale: `DataSource.cache_key` is explicitly shared across agents, and `DatasetManager` stores Redis entries under `dataset:{source.cache_key}`; in-memory keys are also only name-based. A finance result cache keyed only by source or metric can cross tenants, models, periods, or PBAC contexts. Disable result caching initially or include tenant, subject/policy, model hash, resolved chart hash, request, and target in the key.

suggestions.title: Define a separate durable accounting audit contract
suggestions.rationale: `AuditLedgerEntry` is credential-invocation shaped, includes a generated timestamp, and `AuditLedger.append` logs storage failures while retaining only an in-memory record. It cannot prove the exact request, resolved account membership, tenant/subject context, or SQL/model hashes. Reuse the signer interfaces but define a versioned `AccountingAuditEntry` and make the durable-audit failure policy explicit for finance results.

suggestions.title: Separate structural assertion validation from live reconciliation
suggestions.rationale: Metric references, cycles, and expression typing can be validated at model load, but `revenue - expenses == net_income` is a data assertion and cannot be proven until execution. Define assertion status, tolerance, null/no-row behavior, grain, and period alignment; test that failed assertions are surfaced or block results according to an explicit policy.

suggestions.title: Resolve ownership of the parrot.semantic satellite before creating it
suggestions.rationale: The repository has no current `ai-parrot-semantic` package, while the existing semantic-layer specification defines that same satellite as the home of a sidemantic-based generic layer and its packaging/CI boundary. Creating a dependency-free accounting skeleton under the same distribution needs an explicit layering contract so FEAT-704 cannot later redefine or import around it.
